description:
Source: claude-bootstrap-protocol plan Part II task T030 (bead claude-bootstrap-protocol-401.3, blocked on this one). Parent PRD there: .claude/docs/prd.md Part II FR-019, FR-020, FR-022 (Tab 4), FR-024; decision brief decisions 1, 7. ADR 0008 in that kit (global packs) is the mechanism being mirrored.
Triage: backlog (filed from the Claude kit; run refine-beads here before claiming)
Classification: size/cynefin/persona/layer = TBD (refine-beads)
Effort Forecast: TBD (refine-beads)

## Summary

Give the Codex kit the same operator-global install path the Claude kit is adding, so both kits stay symmetric, and provision the Codex side of the two-model review gate. Four deliverables, which refine-beads may split into children:

1. **Global packs for `~/.codex/`.** A pack may carry a `global/` tree beside (or instead of) `scaffold/`; `./bootstrap --global-only --pack <name>` installs it into `~/.codex/` (skills under `~/.codex/skills/<name>/`), tracked by a per-pack stamp file, refreshed on later runs with consent and backup, removed with `--remove-global-pack <name>`. Mirror of claude-bootstrap-protocol T021–T023 (see that repo's `.claude/docs/project-plan.md` Part II for the acceptance criteria to mirror).
2. **`craft` pack.** The same 16 skills and `references/` directory vendored from `addyosmani/agent-skills` at commit `1be8e34` (v0.6.12, MIT), byte-identical except recorded patches, installed into `~/.codex/skills/`. Roster and exclusions: incremental-implementation, api-and-interface-design, frontend-ui-engineering, source-driven-development, doubt-driven-development, debugging-and-error-recovery, browser-testing-with-devtools, code-review-and-quality, code-simplification, security-and-hardening, performance-optimization, ci-cd-and-automation, observability-and-instrumentation, shipping-and-launch, deprecation-and-migration, constraint-driven-development. Excluded: using-agent-skills, interview-me, idea-refine, spec-driven-development, planning-and-task-breakdown, test-driven-development, git-workflow-and-versioning, context-engineering, documentation-and-adrs, and all nine upstream commands.
3. **QA reviewer provisioning.** In `~/.codex/config.toml` a `[profiles.qa]` block with `model = "gpt-6-astra"` and `model_reasoning_effort = "high"`; defaults untouched. Extend the existing `~/.codex/agents/reviewer.toml` (sandbox_mode read-only, report-only) with four passes: acceptance (against the bead's acceptance criteria), code quality, security (auth, input handling, secrets, dependencies, error paths, trust boundaries), regression; and the report shape the Claude side parses: a first line `VERDICT: PASS | FAIL | BLOCKED`, then `Reviewed commit: <sha>`, then findings each with severity (Critical, Important, Nit), file and line, verification or reproduction steps, impact, suggested correction; then `Checks run:` and `Checks not performed:` lists. The Claude side invokes `codex exec --profile qa --sandbox read-only "<prompt naming the commit>"` and treats a missing profile as BLOCKED.
4. **`herdr-qa` wrapper** at `~/.local/bin/herdr-qa` (installed by the kit, symlinked like the bootstrap script): `herdr-qa /abs/path/to/project` launches interactive Codex in that directory with `--profile qa` and the reviewer instructions loaded through a supported mechanism (verify flags against `codex --help` on the installed version, 0.162.1 at filing time; do not invent flags); `exec`s so herdr detects the process as Codex; reads `HERDR_TEAM_MANIFEST` when set and instructs the session to read it plus `~/.claude/skills/herdr-team/PROTOCOL.md` if present; `herdr-qa --check <dir>` validates configuration (profile present, model available, reviewer file present) without starting a model session. Paths with spaces are safe. Fails clearly when the profile or reviewer is absent.

Why now: the Claude kit's review gate (its T029) reports BLOCKED and its team launcher (T035) reports Tab 4 missing until this lands; its live trial (T036) is blocked on it.

## Persona

Primary: Operator (runs both kits; wants one install path per kit and one reviewer contract)
Secondary: Developer (the Claude-side skills that call `codex exec --profile qa` and `herdr-qa`)

## Acceptance Criteria

### Operator
- [ ] `./bootstrap --global-only --pack craft` (this kit) installs the 16 skills and references under `~/.codex/skills/` into a temp `CODEX_HOME`, a second run reports zero changes, and `--remove-global-pack craft` removes exactly the stamped files.
- [ ] `codex --profile qa` reports model `gpt-6-astra` at high reasoning effort; `codex` without the profile is unchanged before and after.
- [ ] `herdr-qa --check <dir>` passes with the profile and reviewer present and fails naming the missing piece otherwise; `herdr-qa <dir>` from a herdr shell pane is detected by `herdr agent list` as `codex`.

### Developer
- [ ] `codex exec --profile qa --sandbox read-only` on a sample commit returns a report in the shape above with no working-tree change.
- [ ] The Claude kit's T029 BLOCKED path no longer triggers on this machine (verified by running its `review-gate codex <commit>` once it exists).

## Scope Boundaries

- In scope: the four deliverables above and their docs in this kit.
- NOT in scope: any change to the Claude kit or `~/.claude/`; vendoring upstream Define/Plan skills; scanning or vetting pipeline work.
- Completion condition: all boxes checked; link this bead's closing comment from claude-bootstrap-protocol-401.3.

## Context to Read

- claude-bootstrap-protocol: `.claude/docs/prd.md` Part II FR-019, FR-020, FR-022, FR-024; `.claude/docs/project-plan.md` Part II T021–T023 (mechanism to mirror), T029 (prompt and report shape), T035 (what the launcher expects from `herdr-qa`); `.claude/docs/adr/0008-*.md`.
- This kit: `bootstrap`, `lib/plan-engine.sh`, the global-install path if one exists, `~/.codex/config.toml`, `~/.codex/agents/reviewer.toml`, `codex --help`, `herdr --skill`.

## Testing Strategy

- Temp `CODEX_HOME` for every install test; never the operator's real config in automated checks.
- `codex --help` flag verification recorded in the bead before the wrapper is written.
- Hazard check: `~/.codex/config.toml` is live operator config; back it up before editing and add only the profile block.

## Dependencies

None in this kit. Upstream contract owner: claude-bootstrap-protocol-401.3.

comments.text:
Refinement from the Claude kit orchestrator (2026-10-12), operator decision B: build herdr-qa properly here so the Claude kit's attended trial (T036) can run its QA tab. Phase 1 (this bead, now): deliverables 3 and 4 only. Phase 2 (deliverables 1 global packs for ~/.codex and 2 craft mirror) is split to a follow-up bead.
Corrections from the Claude kit's T029 (verified against Codex 0.162): profiles live in $CODEX_HOME/<name>.config.toml layered on config.toml; Codex refuses --profile qa when config.toml holds a [profiles.qa] table or profile = "qa". So provision $CODEX_HOME/qa.config.toml with model = "gpt-6-astra", model_reasoning_effort = "high", sandbox_mode = "read-only"; never add [profiles.qa] to config.toml. The Claude kit's review_gate.py profile_check and tools/herdr-team expect exactly that (see claude-bootstrap-protocol assets/packs/craft/global/.claude/references/craft-pack-notes.md 'Manual Codex setup').
herdr-qa contract the Claude launcher (claude-bootstrap-protocol tools/herdr-team on feature/T035-herdr-launcher) relies on: (a) herdr-qa --check <dir>: exit 0 when codex is installed, $CODEX_HOME/qa.config.toml exists with a model line, no legacy profile in config.toml, and agents/reviewer.toml exists; otherwise non-zero with the last line naming what to fix; starts no model session; (b) herdr-qa --help lists --no-alt-screen; (c) herdr-qa <abs-dir> [--no-alt-screen] execs interactive codex in <dir> with --profile qa (and --no-alt-screen passed through to codex when given; verify codex 0.162 flag names with codex --help, do not invent flags), loading the reviewer instructions through a supported mechanism, and when HERDR_TEAM_MANIFEST is set tells the session to read it and ~/.claude/skills/herdr-team/PROTOCOL.md if present. Paths with spaces safe. Installed by this kit's bootstrap into ~/.local/bin (symlink like the bootstrap script), with the qa profile and the reviewer.toml extension, under the kit's existing consent/backup rules for ~/.codex; tests use a temp HOME and CODEX_HOME only.
Bar: practical and functional.

3. `$atlas-doctor` runs the shared script with client `codex`, additionally checks `[features] multi_agent = true` in `$CODEX_HOME/config.toml` and the REA entry `[mcp_servers.rea]`, detects an unstamped `~/.agents/skills/archify` or `graphify` (D-4) and prints the move line. - [ ] The 16 names are available under `$` with implicit invocation off (13 on the first round; rea-binary, rea-android and rea-electron follow when the Claude kit's T048 merges).
- [ ] `$atlas-doctor` reports `multi_agent` and leaves `~/.codex/config.toml` unchanged.
- [ ] A live session shows no implicit invocation (A-011, R-021): an operator step after the real install (T054), not done by the developer.

## Scope Boundaries

No install into the real `~/.agents` or `~/.codex`. No change to the Claude kit's source text: a Command-text fix is made there and re-derived here with the converter.
